title: Intoxication and Altered States in the Greek and Roman World
description: Examines altered states and the chemical, ritual, and visionary means used to attain them in the Greek and Roman world ca. 1500 BC–AD 500. Explores their ecological, social, cultural, and spiritual significance through literary, historical, medical, and material sources. Topics may include: wine, opium, cannabis, and other intoxicants; symposia and Bacchanalia; poetic and oracular inspiration; mystery cults and ecstatic practices; dreams and dream interpretation; gnosis and enlightenment; magic, pharmacology, and the ancient drug trade.
notes: Credit will be granted for only one of GRS 302, GRS 326 (if taken in the same topic).
recommendations: One of GRS 101, GRS 102, GRS 381 recommended prior to GRS 302.
